reasoning_content:
The core timer engine (TimerEngine) exists with Phase, TimerConfig, and Tick. The GUI's MainWindow drives this. The guide says that focus rounds are recorded in the DB, and that early-cancelled rounds are also recorded with the elapsed time. The test suite (20 tests) probably covers these. As an additional behavioral verification, I could run a simple end-to-end with the installed app using the POMODORO_DATA_DIR override to verify that settings.json gets written. But that might be overkill.

Let me do one more meaningful check: launch the app using POMODORO_DATA_DIR pointing to a temporary directory, verify that the override works as documented (a documented feature), confirm that the data directory is respected, and then clean up. This validates the override behavior of paths.py through the installed app.

After that, kill the process and Xvfb to clean up.

action.command: cd /workspace && mkdir -p /tmp/pomodoro-data-test && (DISPLAY=:99 POMODORO_DATA_DIR=/tmp/pomodoro-data-test QT_QPA_PLATFORM=xcb nohup ./.venv/bin/pomodoro > /tmp/pomodoro2.log 2>&1 & echo PID2:$!) && sleep 6 && pgrep -af "\.venv/bin/pomodoro" | grep -v pgrep; echo "--- override dir ---"; ls -la /tmp/pomodoro-data-test/; echo "--- log2 ---"; cat /tmp/pomodoro2.log
